method.method_draft: Use an analytic-coordinate route. Read from the image that PS is the top horizontal side of the square and R is directly below S. From the text, set the square side as 10. Place coordinates P = (0,0), S = (10,0), R = (10,-10). The ray PT forms a 75° angle below the positive x-axis, so points on it have form T = a(cos75°, -sin75°). The ray ST forms a 30° angle below the direction from S to P, so points on it have form T = (10 - b cos30°, -b sin30°). Solve these two ray equations for T; equivalently use triangle PST with base PS = 10 and angles 75°, 30°, 75° to get ST = 10. Then from S, vector ST has direction 30° below left, while vector SR is vertical downward of length 10. Thus compute the distance from T to R by the cosine formula or coordinates: TR^2 = 10^2 + 10^2 - 2(10)(10)cos60° = 100, so TR = 10 cm.
